title: PostgreSQL across clouds: recovery point and failover
description: CloudNativePG distributed topology: pg-primary (EKS, archive in S3) and pg-replica (GKE, archive in GCS).

panels.title: Topology: which cloud is the primary
Role of each Cluster
panels.description: Primary: an instance accepts writes. Replica: replica.primary names the other Cluster, and this one replays its archive. No primary: this Cluster should be the primary but no instance accepts writes, as during a failover between its instances or while it is being promoted. Fenced: every instance is stopped (cnpg.io/fencedInstances), as after an unplanned failover. A planned switchover also fences the old primary for a few seconds while it demotes it. A gap means no instance answered.

targets.expr: max by (cluster) (2 * cnpg_collector_fencing_on{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"}) > 0 or max by (cluster) (1 - cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"}) > 0 or (max by (cluster) (cnpg_collector_replica_mode{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"}) == 1) - 1 or max by (cluster) (cnpg_collector_replica_mode{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"}) * 0 + 3

panels.title: PostgreSQL up, per instance
panels.description: Whether each instance's PostgreSQL answers the metrics collector. Killing the primary pod shows here as a gap, then a new pod. A fenced instance stops collecting, so it is shown as fenced rather than by its last reading.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, pod) (2 * cnpg_collector_fencing_on{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"}) > 0 or max by (cluster, pod) (cnpg_collector_up{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"})

panels.title: Recovery point: how much could be lost
How long closed WAL has waited for the archive
panels.description: Per Cluster (pg-primary archives to S3, pg-replica to GCS): how long closed WAL segments have been waiting to be archived, to within the 10s scrape interval, and 0 when none wait. Healthy archiving takes seconds. A line that keeps climbing means the archive isn't accepting WAL, and everything written meanwhile would be lost with this cloud. Not the time since the last archival: an idle database archives nothing for as long as it is idle, so that would climb for no reason. Fenced instances are left out.

targets.expr: (time() - max_over_time(timestamp(max by (cluster) (cnpg_collector_pg_wal_archive_status{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica", value="ready"} unless on (pod) cnpg_collector_fencing_on == 1) == 0)[1h:10s])) * (max by (cluster) (cnpg_collector_pg_wal_archive_status{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica", value="ready"} unless on (pod) cnpg_collector_fencing_on == 1) > bool 0)

panels.title: WAL segments the replica's archive trails the primary's
panels.description: The cross-cloud lag, in 16MiB WAL segments, for the Cluster in replica mode (after a switchover, the other one). It archives each segment after replaying it, so 0 means it has replayed everything the primary archived. The primary's line is always 0: comparing it the other way would only show CloudNativePG's 30s metrics cache.

targets.expr: (scalar(max((cnpg_pg_stat_archiver_last_archived_wal_start_lsn{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"} >= 0 unless cnpg_pg_stat_archiver_last_archived_wal_start_lsn{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"} % 4294967296 == 0))) - max by (cluster) ((cnpg_pg_stat_archiver_last_archived_wal_start_lsn{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"} >= 0 unless cnpg_pg_stat_archiver_last_archived_wal_start_lsn{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"} % 4294967296 == 0))) * on (cluster) (max by (cluster) (cnpg_collector_replica_mode{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica"}) == bool 1)

panels.title: WAL segments waiting to be archived
panels.description: Segments PostgreSQL has closed but not yet archived (archive_status/*.ready). They pile up on the WAL volume while the object store is unreachable, and drain when it is back. Fenced instances are left out: they stop reporting, so their last reading would stay.

targets.expr: max by (cluster) (cnpg_collector_pg_wal_archive_status{cluster=~"pg-primary|pg-replica", value="ready"} unless on (pod) cnpg_collector_fencing_on == 1)

panels.title: Failed archive attempts
panels.description: Failed archive_command runs per minute, per Cluster. Non-zero while the object store is down; CloudNativePG then reports ContinuousArchiving=False.

panels.title: Backups: what each cloud can restore on its own
Last base backup
panels.description: When each archive's newest base backup completed, from the Barman Cloud plugin: pg-primary's in S3, pg-replica's in GCS. Each cloud keeps its own, so either can restore without the other. Backups run when a Cluster is created and nightly at 02:00 UTC: orange after 25 hours, red after 48.

panels.title: Restorable back to
panels.description: The earliest point in time each archive can restore to on its own: its oldest base backup. Everything from there to the last archived WAL segment is recoverable. Moves forward once the 7-day retention policy starts deleting old backups.

panels.title: Rows written per minute in the app database
panels.description: Rows inserted, updated or deleted in the app database, per Cluster. Only the primary writes, so this shows where writes land. DDL counts too: one CREATE TABLE writes dozens of system catalog rows, so the scale is logarithmic: one row a minute stays visible next to it, and minutes with no writes leave a gap. Transaction counts would mislead here: they include read-only queries, the metrics collector's own among them, on replicas too.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster) (increase(cnpg_pg_stat_database_tup_inserted{cluster=~"pg-.*", datname="app"}[1m])) + sum by (cluster) (increase(cnpg_pg_stat_database_tup_updated{cluster=~"pg-.*", datname="app"}[1m])) + sum by (cluster) (increase(cnpg_pg_stat_database_tup_deleted{cluster=~"pg-.*", datname="app"}[1m]))
